# How this profile works (and how to change it)

Every visual on the profile is an **SVG image**. SVGs are just text files (XML), so they are
**generated by Python code** from one config file. You never draw or edit the images by hand.

```
profile.toml  ──►  scripts/generate.py  ──►  SVG images  ──►  README.md shows them
 (your words)        (the "artist")           (assets/ and the `output` branch)
```

## 1. Change words, links, stack, projects  (easiest, no code)

Edit **`profile.toml`**. Then regenerate the committed images:

```bash
python scripts/generate.py --static     # rewrites assets/*.svg
git add -A && git commit -m "Update profile" && git push
```

| I want to change…              | Edit in `profile.toml`                  |
|--------------------------------|------------------------------------------|
| Name, roles, status, typed lines | `[profile]`                             |
| About rows / quote             | `[about]`, `[[about.rows]]`              |
| Tech stack chips               | `[[stack]]`                              |
| Email / LinkedIn / GitHub      | `[links]`                                |
| Which 4 repos are shown        | `[featured] repos = [...]`               |
| Number of languages shown      | `[languages]`                            |

The **live cards** (contribution grid, numbers, project cards) rebuild themselves every night
and on every push to `main` via `.github/workflows/profile.yml`. You can also run it by hand:
GitHub → Actions → Profile → Run workflow.

## 2. Change how things LOOK  (needs code, or an AI model)

Each card is one small Python file in `scripts/profilegen/cards/`:

| File          | Image it draws                                  |
|---------------|--------------------------------------------------|
| `hero.py`     | Top banner: planet, name, typing line            |
| `section.py`  | The "01 ABOUT" style headings                     |
| `about.py`    | About card                                       |
| `stack.py`    | Tech stack chips                                 |
| `activity.py` | Contribution grid + streaks (live data)          |
| `stats.py`    | Big numbers + language bar (live data)           |
| `project.py`  | One repo card (live data)                        |
| `connect.py`  | Closing "Let's build something" card             |

Colours live in **one place**: `scripts/profilegen/theme.py` (dark and light palettes, all greys).
Shared helpers (fonts, escaping, text wrapping): `scripts/profilegen/svg.py`.

### Preview before publishing
```bash
python scripts/generate.py --sample rich --out preview      # fake data, no internet needed
```
Open any `preview/*.svg` in a browser. Animations play in the browser.

### Check nothing broke
```bash
python -m unittest discover -s tests -t .
```
The tests also fail if `assets/` is out of date, which reminds you to run `--static`.

## 3. Ask an AI model to redesign something

Give the AI this repo (or the zip) plus a prompt like:

> This repo generates a GitHub profile from Python code that outputs SVG files. Read `EDITING.md`
> first. I want to change **[the hero banner / the stack card / ...]** to **[describe what you want]**.
> Rules: edit only the relevant file in `scripts/profilegen/cards/`; keep everything strictly
> black/white/grey using colours from `theme.py` (the tests enforce this); keep it working in both
> dark and light themes; keep animations CSS/SMIL only (no JavaScript, GitHub strips it); use only
> the Python standard library. When done, run the tests and
> `python scripts/generate.py --static`, then show me what changed.

## Good to know

- GitHub shows SVGs through `<img>`, so **no JavaScript**, and no web fonts. Fonts are system stacks
  defined in `svg.py`.
- Images can't contain clickable links. Links are in `README.md` around the images.
- Dark/light: every card is rendered twice (`-dark.svg`, `-light.svg`); `README.md` uses `<picture>`
  so GitHub picks the right one for the viewer's theme.
- Live cards are published to the `output` branch (a single force-pushed commit, no history).
